key_insight: Independent reproduction and external benchmarking indicate that RXNGraphormer is reliable and transferable for reaction prediction, but its performance drops in heterogeneous or distribution-shifted datasets. In short, the model is reproducible, yet its robustness has limits when applied beyond its original data conditions.
problem_solved: This paper evaluates whether a reaction prediction model can be independently reproduced and whether it generalizes well to external datasets under realistic, shifting data conditions.
method: Independently reproduced the RXNGraphormer results to assess reproducibility.
Tested the model on external benchmark datasets for reaction prediction tasks.
Compared performance across standard, heterogeneous, and distribution-shifted settings to assess transferability.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this study provides a practical check on model reliability beyond published results. It highlights the importance of external validation before deployment, especially in scientific applications where data distribution can change.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing reproduction plus external evaluation
Side-by-side bar chart comparing performance on original vs external datasets
Shift/robustness heatmap illustrating performance under distribution shift
Simple icon set for reproducibility, transferability, and robustness
paper_title: Reusability report: Assessment of reproducibility and applicability to external datasets for RXNGraphormer
paper_authors: Chonghuan Zhang, Majian Zeng, Qianghua Lin, Kuangbiao Liao
